data.reasoning: The package contains standard AUR packaging files. The PKGBUILD downloads from an official upstream mirror, uses PGP signature verification, and contains no malicious top-level code or suspicious build/package functions. The other files are standard metadata and configuration. The 'inconclusive' verdict from one model was solely due to a transient API error, not a security finding.
data.disagreement_analysis: The disagreement was caused by a tool error (HTTP 400 BadRequestError) in the qwen model when attempting to audit the PKGBUILD and lyxrc.dist files, forcing an inconclusive verdict. The deepseek model successfully audited these files and correctly identified them as safe.
coverage_issues: qwen model failed to audit PKGBUILD and lyxrc.dist due to an LLM API error (HTTP 400).
learnings: Transient API errors (e.g., HTTP 400) during file audits should trigger automatic retries or fallback to other models rather than immediately resulting in an inconclusive package verdict.
Distinguish between security disagreements and tool failures when triggering escalation audits to avoid unnecessary overhead.
